comment: Baseline numbers for the research-mode stabilization work. Read alongside
docs/regression_baseline_2026-07-28.md, which explains what each number means.
Nothing here is a target -- it is the state the diagnostic-detail patch was
measured against, so a later run can be compared to it instead of to memory.

pre_gate_failure_comment: Counted per strict leg from manifest.jsonl, NOT from failures_by_code.txt.
That report counts distinct papers across both modes, so it credits
processes_required with a paper whose strict leg actually died at the gates,
and files no_reactions separately as an uncoded failure_kind.

comment: Same paper, two runs twelve hours apart. The 09:19 strict leg passed with a
4.7 MB merged payload; the 21:22 strict leg failed with a 306 KB one -- a
15.37x shrink. This is why fixtures here are curated by hand: one merged
payload is larger than the entire test suite's fixture budget.
Figures are os.path.getsize() on the artifacts, i.e. true filesystem bytes.
The manifest's own file sizes are decoded-character counts and read low on
any payload carrying non-ASCII -- these are UTF-8 with Greek letters in the
entity names, so the two differ by roughly 1%.
Full offline suite on research-mode, run with an explicit --basetemp (see docs).
Recorded, not asserted: adding a test must not fail the harness.
